The statement conveys a cautiously supportive tone: the FOMC delivered a modest 25 bp cut to 4.5–4.75% while reaffirming QT caps ($25B Treasuries, $35B MBS reinvested into Treasuries) and adjusting administered rates (IORB 4.65%, ON RRP 4.55%). In a forward‑looking rules framework (Clarida, Galí, and Gertler; Taylor rule), a small cut amid “balanced” risks and easing labor tightness is consistent with flexible inflation‑forecast targeting (Svensson and Woodford) while inflation is still “somewhat elevated.” The continued balance‑sheet runoff and corridor/floor implementation via interest on reserves (Goodfriend) help prevent an over‑loosening of financial conditions. Standard transmission evidence (Christiano, Eichenbaum, and Evans) implies the rate cut should support demand with lags, and the communication effect (Romer and Romer) signals confidence in disinflation progress without declaring victory. Net: mildly positive, tempered by uncertainty and ongoing QT.
